items.title: CIMB keeps "Buy" call on TNB, RM15.90 target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) has guided for a high single-digit equity internal rate of return (IRR) on its hybrid hydro floating solar at Tasik Kenyir after taking into account higher capital expenditure of between 10 and 15 per cent on the project. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said that the solar project in Tasik Kenyir has three benefits, namely increased power output owing to the waterbody's cooling effect, zero land clearing and avoidance of 650,000 tonnes of annual carbon dioxide emissions. Meanwhile, TNB's Sungai Perak's Hydro Life Extension Programme will rehabilitate and upgrade TNB's ageing Sungai Perak hydroelectric plant, covering five hydro stations with a combined installed capacity of 648 megawatts.

items.title: Trading landscape evolving
items.summary: Olive Tree Property Consultants founder Samuel Tan said the shift towards web-based trading reflects changing expectations among traders, who increasingly want to manage their accounts across different devices without being tied to a dedicated trading workstation. JustMarkets, a multi-asset CFD broker, said browser-based trading removes one of the basic barriers to accessing markets — the need to install trading software. The spokesperson said web-based trading platforms have also evolved beyond providing basic access to trading accounts.

items.title: Teen drowns in Klang lake, Bomba recovers body after two‑hour search
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — A 15-year-old boy drowned while swimming in a lake in Bandar Botanik, Klang yesterday. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 6.21pm. He said the search operation involved seven personnel from the Andalas station, assisted by the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) from the Shah Alam station.

items.title: Saudi coalition accuses Houthis of drone strike on holy city Madinah
items.summary: RIYADH: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis struck an electricity distribution station in the holy city of Madinah in Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition said Thursday, sparking strong condemnation from the Muslim world. The Saudi-led coalition said a drone struck Madinah's Taibah electricity distribution station, which provides power to the Prophet's Mosque, as the Houthis denied involvement. Al-Maliki said the facility supplied electricity to the Prophet's Mosque.

items.title: Penampang floods force 118 victims into four relief centres
items.summary: The flooding affected 15 villages, including Kampung Penampang Proper, Kampung Kolopis, Kampung Sarapung, Kampung Dabak, Kampung Tanaki, Kampung Pagansakan, Kampung Nambazan, Kampung Huba and Kampung Kibabaig. The affected areas also include Kampung Limbanak, Kampung Penampang Kondis, Kampung Sugud, Kampung Pinapah, Vista Kiranau and Kampung Kambau. Twelve roads are affected but remain passable, including Jalan Tanaki-Bandason, Jalan Vista Kiranau, Jalan Inobong, Jalan Kampung Putaton, Pagansakan Bridge, Jalan Sarapung, Jalan Kolopis-Boliga and Jalan Bantazon-Kolopis.

items.title: Tampin tragedy: Cable snag topples utility pole, killing motorcyclist, police detain lorry driver
items.summary: TAMPIN, Oct 2 — An elderly man was killed after a utility pole fell on him at Felda Jelai here yesterday. He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was travelling from Felda Jelai 3 towards the Felda Jelai Health Clinic, while the lorry was believed to have been exiting a junction from Felda Jelai 4. He said the victim sustained serious head injuries and died while receiving treatment at the Felda Jelai Health Clinic.

items.title: Most areas record moderate air quality amid transboundary haze
items.summary: Data from APIMS showed that 67 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings. In Selangor, air quality monitoring stations in Shah Alam, Klang, Johan Setia, Petaling Jaya, Kuala Selangor and Banting recorded moderate API readings. Only five air quality monitoring stations, mostly in Sarawak and Sabah, recorded good API readings.

items.title: Bukit Aman confirms arrests: Eight police personnel held over ketum water activities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Eight police personnel were among nine individuals arrested on suspicion of being involved in ketum water-related activities during a raid in Taman Keramat here on Sept 29. Bukit Aman Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS) director Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid confirmed the arrests. “Yes, Bukit Aman JIPS confirms the arrest of eight police personnel along with a civilian in an operation in Taman Keramat,” she said when contacted.

items.title: Man City should face consequences if guilty, says UK PM spokesperson
items.summary: LONDON: Manchester City should face the "appropriate consequences" if wrongdoing is established, a spokesperson for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Thursday, a day after he expressed concern about City's owners potentially selling the club. The club have denied wrongdoing and said they will appeal. "Andy Burnham's intervention in support of Manchester City's owners is frankly extraordinary.

items.title: Police say plan ahead: Five checkpoints, contra‑flow lanes and diversions as Sepang braces for F1 crowds
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — All vehicles heading to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) for the 2026 Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix will undergo screening at five main locations to ensure smooth traffic flow throughout the event. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the locations are the route from the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) toll plaza towards Jalan Pekeliling; from KLIA1 towards Jalan Pekeliling; before the Masjid Roundabout towards SIC; from Kota Warisan towards Labohan Dagang and Jalan KLIA1; and the junction of Jalan Kuarters KLIA towards SIC at the Enstek traffic lights. Shazeli said 365 officers and personnel from the Selangor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) would be deployed for traffic control, congestion prevention patrols, law enforcement and VIP escort duties throughout the event.

items.title: ‘Every corner reminds him of her’: Mukhriz appeals for privacy for Dr Mahathir
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir has appealed to the public and the media to give his father, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, the necessary time and privacy to grieve following the passing of his beloved wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. He said that being inside the family home has been emotionally difficult for the 101-year-old Dr Mahathir, as nearly every room brings back poignant memories of his late wife. For that reason, Mukhriz said that it is preferable for Dr Mahathir to remain temporarily at the National Heart Institute (IJN) until his physical and emotional strength improves.

items.title: Indonesia battles raging fires as 72ha remain ablaze
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia continues to battle forest and land fires across four provinces, with fires still affecting over 72ha. National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Disaster Data, Information and Communication Centre acting head Berton Panjaitan said the remaining affected areas were in South Sumatra, Central Kalimantan, Jambi and West Kalimantan as of Wednesday. South Sumatra had the largest area still requiring firefighting efforts at 28.5ha, followed by Central Kalimantan with 27.6ha, Jambi with 14ha and West Kalimantan with 2.34ha, he said.

items.title: Anwar tells Bahrain crown prince Malaysia is revved up to host Formula 1 Grand Prix
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday shared updates on the preparations for the 2026 Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa. Also present were Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif and Bahrain International Circuit (BIC) chief executive Sheikh Salman Isa Al Khalifa. SIC was chosen to host the 2026 Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, making the iconic circuit a temporary venue for the prestigious race.

items.title: Singapore to face hot weather, thunderstorms in early October
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Hot weather and thunderstorms are expected over parts of Singapore in the first half of October as the Southwest Monsoon continues over the region, the Meteorological Service Singapore said on Thursday. Daily maximum temperatures are likely to range between 34 degrees Celsius and 35 degrees Celsius on most days and could slightly exceed 35 degrees Celsius on a few days. Some nights may also remain warm and humid, with minimum temperatures above 27 degrees Celsius.

items.title: Court of Appeal upholds ex-Umany president's conviction for insulting former UM vice-chancellor
items.summary: Court of Appeal judge Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, who led a three-member panel, said Wong had the right to speak out, criticise and express disagreement, but not to disregard the law. "The court is punishing your conduct based on the court's finding that you have exceeded the limits set by the law. Noorin said this in her judgment after the appellate court dismissed Wong's appeal against his conviction and RM10,000 fine for insulting a former Universiti Malaya vice-chancellor.

items.title: Woman killed after being struck by car while lying on road
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 39-year-old mentally disabled woman was killed after she was struck by a car while lying in the middle of the road along Jalan Jambatan Sultan Mahmud early today. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said police were alerted to the incident at 2.15am. "Upon reaching the location, the car struck the victim, Ainun Wahab, who was lying in the middle of the road.

items.title: Equities rebound to close higher as surging Treasury yields recede
items.summary: NEW YORK: US stocks recovered from early losses to close slightly higher on Thursday, with the S&P 500 bouncing from a two-week low as a global bond selloff reversed course after sending US Treasury yields to multi-decade highs. Treasury yields extended gains, and the benchmark 10-year Treasury note hit a 24-year high, after closing out September with its biggest quarterly gain since 1994, and pushed equities lower after the Institute for Supply Management said its manufacturing PMI dipped to 54.5 last month from 54.6 in August and showed a jump in input prices, raising inflation worries. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 20.69 points, or 0.04 per cent, to 50,926.74, the S&P 500 gained 14.94 points, or 0.20 per cent, to 7,666.48 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 10.53 points, or 0.04 per cent, to 26,871.60.

items.title: Clear skies for F1, KL Marathon as air quality improves nationwide; Seri Manjung sole hotspot
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Malaysia is heading into a bumper weekend of major international and national sporting events with clear skies across almost the entire country, as only a single monitoring station recorded unhealthy air quality this morning. Every other monitoring station across Malaysia recorded moderate or good air quality with readings of 100 or below, providing timely relief for organisers, athletes, and tens of thousands of spectators ahead of a packed sports calendar. The cleared conditions mean flagship events, including the Formula One race at the Sepang International Circuit, Le Tour de Langkawi, and the Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon, are set to proceed as scheduled.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah highlights upbeat Malaysia–Singapore talks as ministerial committee meets Nov 2 on economic zone plan
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — The first meeting of the Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee (JSCMC) will be held in Singapore on Nov 2. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the matter was discussed during a meeting with Singapore Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry Gan Kim Yong at his office here yesterday. Akmal Nasrullah said the JS-SEZ has significant potential, with more than S$5.5 billion (RM17.97 billion) in investment commitments from Singapore-based companies recorded as of October 2025.

items.title: Experts call for ‘Ministry of Longevity’ to prepare Malaysia for aged nation status
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Malaysia should coordinate efforts and policies when it comes to longevity and older people, by getting the government, businesses and civil society to work together, National Council of Women's Organisations (NCWO) Malaysia president Prof. Emerita Tan Sri Dr Sharifah Hapsah Syed Hasan has proposed. Dr Sharifah said there is a need to have a coordinating body, adding that it is up to the federal government on how this body would operate, such as as a council or committee. She said the proposed coordinating body would look at policies on creating a society that will not only live longer but also put life to age, and also at all aspects of a longer life.

items.title: Thailand intensifies flood response ahead of Oct 4-5 heavy rain
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand is stepping up its flood response ahead of heavy rain forecast for Oct 4 to 5, with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul ordering emergency assistance for vulnerable groups. Anutin, who is also interior minister, said under the government's "leave no one behind" approach, authorities were ordered to ensure timely assistance for the elderly, bedridden patients, children and people with disabilities. "Authorities should accelerate assistance to affected people nationwide and survey households that still lack essential supplies, particularly vulnerable groups," he said after a meeting of the National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Command on Thursday.

items.title: #NSTviral: Will Malaysians change? School crossing video raises concerns
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Concerns over motorists failing to give way to pedestrians have resurfaced after schoolchildren were seen struggling to cross a zebra crossing. The video, believed to have been recorded near Sekolah Kebangsaan Putrajaya Presint 9(2), shows two children attempting to cross while motorcycles and cars continue passing. Threads user shahrimtamrin, who shared the video, asked: "When will Malaysians change?

items.title: UM to roll out hostel project housing 40,000 students, meeting B40 families’ needs, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Universiti Malaya (UM) will provide accommodation for more than 40,000 students through the Student Residential Hostel Project, which is expected to be launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 15. Meanwhile, UM vice-chancellor Datuk Seri Prof Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman said the project would be implemented in two phases, with the first providing accommodation for 10,000 students and the second for 30,000. In another development, Noor Azuan said ILMUcode was the first artificial intelligence (AI)-based coding platform introduced at UM, enabling developers and students to access advanced coding capabilities at a lower cost.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against greenback, major currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and most major currencies on Friday, supported by stronger demand for the local currency despite firmer US economic data that strengthened the greenback. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0820/0885 against the US dollar from Thursday's close of 4.0830/4.0875. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Institute for Supply Management Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index was at 54.5 points in September, compared with 54.6 points in the previous month.

items.title: Netanyahu claims flydubai co-pilot was 'radicalised' as UAE probes terror link
items.summary: DUBAI: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Thursday the co-pilot behind an attack on a flight to Israel had undergone "radical indoctrination" as the United Arab Emirates said it was probing a possible terror link. The dramatic events on Wednesday saw passengers reroute the flydubai plane to stop it from crashing, making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia before the flight's mostly Israeli passengers were flown home to a hero's welcome. Netanyahu told Fox News.

items.title: Anwar vows tighter governance as Madani Government moves to seal leaks and abuse of power
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The government will continue to strengthen public service governance and integrity to combat the leakage of public funds and abuse of power, particularly involving Federal Statutory Bodies, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the meeting also agreed for a legal study to be conducted to draft the policy, governance direction and the Charities Bill to regulate trust entities and public funding. Anwar said the Madani Government will continue to strengthen public service integrity and close any avenues for leakages and abuse of power.

items.title: Fed policymakers lean against October rate hike
items.summary: NEW YORK: Two of the Federal Reserve's top policymakers this week staked out an unusually clear case for taking in more data before deciding about another interest-rate hike, driving investors to largely abandon bets on an interest rate increase at the central bank's next policy meeting, in late October. "One further upward adjustment" in the policy rate may be appropriate late this year, said Williams, who is also vice chair of the central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee. Fed policymakers projected one more rate hike this year.

items.title: RM4 apam balik draws customers from across Johor
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A family recipe that has been passed down for 19 years continues to keep customers coming back for the Jalan Mawai "apam balik" here. Nelta Efrida Zulfadhli, 37, said all ingredients were prepared fresh daily, with the flour batter made at the premises and the corn prepared in-house instead of being sourced from cans. She said daily sales reached as high as RM6,000 when her "apam balik" went viral.

items.title: Trump vows to hit Iran 'very hard' if linked to flydubai attack
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that Teheran was likely involved in an attack by a pilot on a flydubai flight to Israel and that Iran would be "hit very hard" if it was. On whether the United States would retaliate against Iran if it was responsible for the attack, Trump replied: "Oh, they'll be hit very hard, don't worry." It's possible," Trump told Time.

items.title: Man dies after falling from apartment, police seek witnesses
items.summary: Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report on the incident at 3.46pm. "A team from the Forensic Unit deployed to the scene found the victim lying face down and he was pronounced dead," he said in a statement. He said an examination of the victim's body found no evidence of foul play.

items.title: OpenAI fires three researchers over mishandling of 'sensitive' information
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said Thursday that it has fired three researchers for allegedly mishandling "sensitive information" and violating company policies, including work that involved an external organisation that evaluates artificial intelligence models. "We have parted ways with three individuals," OpenAI told AFP in a statement. The three researchers fired by OpenAI are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, according to the WSJ.

items.title: Everyone can be replaced at work
items.summary: THERE is an uncomfortable truth about the workplace that many people do not like to hear: everyone can be replaced. People leave, organisations restructure, technology advances, responsibilities shift and new talent arrives. Too often, people confuse being valuable with being indispensable.

items.title: Borrowing appetite cools among Malaysian households, business loans hold up
items.summary: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said household loan growth eased marginally to 5.0 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in August from 5.1 per cent in July. Household loan applications contracted 5.1 per cent, reversing a 1.7 per cent increase previously, while approvals fell 10.4 per cent, compared with a 2.4 per cent decline in July. Securities grew 2.8 per cent, while deposits rose 2.3 per cent.

items.title: Decision-making: Malaysia's next competitive advantage
items.summary: IN a business entity, a great customer opportunity had presented itself. The decision had to pass through several layers before anyone could act. And the organisation was left wondering what went wrong.

items.title: US female inmate survives botched execution after two lethal injections, in critical condition
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A condemned female murderer who survived two lethal injections during a botched execution by the US state of Tennessee was in critical condition and receiving "life-saving care," her lawyer said Thursday. In an extraordinary chain of events, Christa Pike, 50, was whisked from a prison execution chamber to a hospital Wednesday night, still alive despite two deadly doses of pentobarbital. Experts on the US death penalty said the case was unprecedented.

items.title: Trump launches midterm campaign blitz as Republicans face tough races
items.summary: DENTON: President Donald Trump began a 32-day campaign blitz on Thursday with stops in Texas and Oklahoma, aiming to bolster Republican candidates as his party fights to hold onto its slim congressional majorities in November's midterm elections. Trump wants to be the face of the party's midterm effort and plans to campaign in a number of competitive House of Representatives and Senate races, at a time that some Republican candidates are unsure whether that will help or hurt them. HEAVY SPENDING Texas is among eight US Senate races rated competitive.

items.title: Nike plans job cuts as sales forecast points to further decline
items.summary: NEW YORK: Nike plans to cut an undetermined number of jobs and establish a new campus in India as it seeks to accelerate a turnaround following another downcast quarter. Nike reported a two per cent drop in quarterly profits to US$712 million. Revenues fell four per cent to US$11.2 billion for the quarter ending August 31, the first quarter of Nike's fiscal 2027.

items.title: Experts warn PM2.5 fine particles pose health risks to vulnerable groups
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prolonged exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) can pose serious health risks beyond respiratory problems, particularly among vulnerable groups. Malaysian Environmental Health Practitioners Association chairman Prof Dr Jamal Hisham Hashim said a 2024 study in The Lancet Planetary Health found that about a million premature deaths globally each year were attributable to short-term exposure to PM2.5 lasting several hours to days. Dr Jamal said prolonged exposure was particularly concerning for vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly and people with chronic respiratory and cardiovascular conditions.

items.title: Doctors fear haze's long-term effects [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: General practitioners (GPs) are seeing more patients with respiratory complaints, but private hospitals say they are coping with the haze for now. Federation of Private Medical Practitioners' Associations president Dr G. Shanmuganathan said GPs were seeing more patients with symptoms associated with poor air quality. Meanwhile, Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said private hospitals were not seeing any significant increase in admissions linked to the haze.

items.title: US judge denies Lindsay Clancy's acquittal bid over deaths of three children
items.summary: During the trial, 36-year-old Lindsay Clancy did not deny strangling Cora, age five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months. Judge William Sullivan, of the Plymouth court near Boston, ruled there was sufficient evidence to convince a juror of Clancy's guilt. said Reddington previously.

items.title: Electricity bill protection up to 800kWh: What does it mean for a household?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The government has expanded electricity bill protection to domestic users consuming up to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month, up from the previous 600kWh limit. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government expanded electricity bill protection to households using up to 800kWh a month. A kilowatt-hour, or kWh, is a unit used to measure how much electricity you use.

items.title: Pentagon signs US$24.4bil deal to accelerate missile output
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Pentagon on Thursday announced the award of a US$24.4 billion contract for Raytheon to accelerate production of SM-6 missiles as Washington works to replace the large amount of munitions expended during the Iran war. The missiles are "critical anti-air and anti-surface warfare munition. This five-year agreement, with two additional option years, will drive faster production," the Pentagon said in a statement.

items.title: MACC remands brothers with ‘Datuk Seri’, ‘Datuk Wira’ titles over alleged RM10m investment abuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Two corporate figures, who are brothers, have been remanded for five days over an alleged abuse of position involving an investment of about RM10 million. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained the remand order, effective today until October 5, from Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning. The MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash.

items.title: Johor rolls out additional RM30m after flash floods hit state capital
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will provide an additional allocation of RM30 million next year to fund four urgent measures to address flash flooding in the state capital. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the allocation aims to fast-track the implementation of short- and medium-term measures to tackle flash floods. Also present were Johor Bahru Mayor Datuk Mohd Haffiz Ahmad and Perling assemblyman P. Pannir Selvam.

items.title: Johor government to enhance ‘Smart City’ technology for early extreme weather warnings
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will enhance its ‘Smart City’ technology to enable city residents to receive early flood warnings during extreme heavy rain that poses a risk of flash floods. State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the early flood warning alerts or notifications would be sent directly to mobile phones via a smart application. Mohd Jafni explained that two flood warning sirens were operational during yesterday’s flash flood incident, with each sounding three times.

items.title: Bidor petrol station shooting: Police record nine statements, hunt three suspects
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 1 — Perak police have recorded statements from nine people, including the victim, in their investigation into the shooting of a businessman at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral last Tuesday. Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those whose statements were recorded included three family members who were in the victim’s vehicle, two people in a vehicle near the scene and employees of the petrol station. He said the victim is now in stable condition after receiving treatment and undergoing surgery at Seri Botani Hospital, while police are investigating from various angles, including identifying the motive, which has yet to be established.

items.title: Petronas-Sarawak oil and gas dispute heads to Federal Court for five-day hearing from Jan 25
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Federal Court has set five days from January 25 next year to hear petitions filed by Petroliam National Bhd (Petronas) and the Sarawak Government challenging the state and federal laws governing oil and gas matters. However, she left it to the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions to decide whether to first hear the Sarawak Government’s preliminary issue on the validity of the Sarawak (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954 (OIC), which concerns the boundaries of Sarawak’s territorial waters. However, the state government maintains that its petition should be heard first.

items.title: Don't abuse your power, deputy IGP tells police
items.summary: Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid said leadership was not a privilege to be used for personal gain but a major trust that must be discharged responsibly. “Therefore, I urge that every decision made must be based on integrity, accountability and a sense of fairness,” he said at the handover ceremony for the Sarawak acting police commissioner and acting chairman of the Sarawak Contingent Persatuan Keluarga Polis (Perkep) at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters here today. Earlier, he witnessed the handover of duties from PDRM Management Department director Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who was also the Sarawak police commissioner, to his deputy DCP Saifullizan Ishak before Mohamad Zainal begins his duties at Bukit Aman.

items.title: Malaysia’s marine police nab 2,707, record 7,627 cases in national waters this year
items.summary: Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said that the success was the result of continuous enforcement through various operations such as Op Taring Gelora, Op Taring Landai, and inter or intra-agency operations. “The highest offences among them involve the Fisheries Act 1985 with 3,214 cases, the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (428), the Control of Supplies Control Act 1961 (295), the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the ATIPSOM Act 2007 (213), as well as the Customs Act 1967 (189 cases),” he said at a press conference after officiating the 79th Anniversary celebration of the PPM at the Region One PPM Operations headquarters, Pulau Indah here today. Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said that PPM as a whole now has 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan (11MP to 13MP) worth RM1.064 billion.

items.title: Malaysia plans A-to-D food grades to nudge manufacturers — and consumers — towards healthier choices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia could introduce a new food labelling system giving packaged food and drinks nutrition grades from A to D by the end of this year, Health Ministry official Dr Yap Wei Aun has said. Dr Yap, chief executive officer of the Health Ministry’s Health Transformation Office, said prevention was a fundamental aspect of public health and cited the proposed labelling system as an example of the government’s preventive health initiatives. Dr Yap said the Health Ministry had been working with partners, including the food industry, to introduce the “front-of-pack labelling” system, under which bottles of drinks or packaged food would carry an A, B, C or D grade.

items.title: Three separate drug busts net RM3.44m in drugs, five arrests in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police arrested five people, including a couple, and seized various types of drugs worth RM3.44 million in three separate operations between September 21 and 27. Penang Police Chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the raids by the state Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) resulted in the seizure of 8.83 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin, 15.06 kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, five litres of liquid MDMA, 182 ecstasy pills and 70 grammes (g) of ketamine. Lim said police seized 3.26 kg of MDMA powder and five litres of liquid MDMA, estimated to be worth RM1.2 million, while investigations found that the couple worked at entertainment centres and obtained the MDMA supply from a drug distribution syndicate.

items.title: F1 fever builds as PM Anwar takes pit-lane walk at Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fever moved up a gear at the Sepang International Circuit today as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined a Pit Lane Walk on the eve of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. This weekend’s race marks Formula 1’s return to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting a world championship round in 2017. Interest has been strong, with nearly 100,000 tickets sold as of Wednesday — a record for races held at the circuit, according to Sepang International Circuit chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Monthly SARA aid credited to recipients’ MyKad from today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid has begun being credited to recipients through their respective MyKad cards from today. The Finance Ministry (MoF), in a post on X today, said RM100 in monthly SARA aid would be credited to households receiving Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), while senior citizens and single individuals would each receive RM50 a month. For recipients of both STR and eKasih, households will receive RM200 in monthly SARA aid, while senior citizens will receive RM150 and single individuals RM100.

items.title: Weather alert: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect several areas in Kedah, namely Kuala Muda, Sik and Baling; Perak, including Hulu Perak, Selama, Kerian, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk; and Kelantan, covering Kuala Krai and Jeli. The same warning was issued for Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Rompin, Maran, Temerloh and Bera in Pahang; and Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Gombak, Petaling, Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, reported Bernama.

items.title: Health Ministry warns against GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after mercury found
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has cancelled the notification of the cosmetic product GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after it was found to contain scheduled poisons, mercury, and is no longer allowed to be sold in the country. Following that, the ministry urged the public to avoid buying and using the involved cosmetics. The statement said that the involved sellers and distributors of the cosmetics must immediately cease the sale and distribution of the cosmetics.

items.title: Indonesia remains a favourite destination for Malaysians as August arrivals jump nearly 29pc
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 1 — Malaysians remained Indonesia’s largest source of foreign tourists in August, with arrivals jumping 28.95 per cent year-on-year to 296,227. According to Statistics Indonesia (BPS), Malaysian visitors accounted for 18.52 per cent of the 1.60 million foreign tourist arrivals recorded during the month. BPS said overall foreign tourist arrivals in August rose 6.27 per cent from a year earlier, while arrivals from January to August reached 10.58 million, up 5.38 per cent from the corresponding period in 2025.

items.title: Kuala Terengganu High Court awards RM47,000 to boy who broke leg after being ‘slammed’ onto chair by teacher
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court today awarded RM47,000 in damages and costs to a boy, now 13, who suffered a broken right leg in an incident involving a Quran and Fardu Ain (KAFA) teacher four years ago. Judge Yusrin Faidz Yusoff allowed Muhammad Izz Anaqi Mohd Izwan’s appeal and set aside an earlier Sessions Court decision that had dismissed his claim, Utusan Malaysia reported. “The judge failed to assess the evidence of two eyewitnesses and the specialist medical report from Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital.

items.title: Anwar thanks outgoing China ambassador for strengthening ties with Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed his appreciation to outgoing Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia, Ouyang Yujing, for his commitment and contribution towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries. Anwar conveyed his appreciation when he received a farewell call from Ouyang today. He said Malaysia and China had built strong ties across various sectors, including the economy, technology, education and culture.

items.title: Selangor employers who chose Sultan’s Silver Jubilee Oct 25 holiday must observe it, says Labour Dept
items.summary: The department said the special public holiday was declared under subsection 9(1) of the Holidays Act 1951 [Act 369], which allows the state government to declare any day as a public holiday in the state. On September 11, the Selangor state government announced October 26 as a replacement public holiday for the entire state following the declaration of October 25 as a special public holiday in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration. Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the replacement holiday was declared because the celebration and the special public holiday fell on a Sunday.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming offers one month’s ministerial salary for top Housing Ministry innovator
items.summary: He said there is ample scope for innovation at the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) as it oversees housing, local government, cleanliness and solid waste management, fire and rescue services, as well as urban planning, all of which have a direct impact on people’s lives. He said this in his speech at the 2026 Ministry of Housing and Local Government Innovation Day (HIKPKT 2026) here today. HIKPKT 2026, themed “ Memperkasa Inovasi, Memacu Prestasi, Menyejahtera Rakyat ”, showcased 54 innovation projects, including 43 Innovative and Creative Group (KIK) projects and 11 Minister’s Innovation Award (AIM) projects.
